lib.intro: Add new downloads, free up space and see what you have.
lib.inbox.title: Add new downloads
lib.inbox.text: Put the CC and mods you download into this folder. Press Add to game and the Hub puts each file in the right place.
lib.inbox.empty: Nothing is waiting. Put new downloads in the folder above, then press Refresh.
lib.cleanup.text: Some CC is stored more than once. The Hub can remove the extra copies. Your game looks the same, and you can undo it on the Tools page.
lib.report.title: Library report
lib.report.text: A one-page overview of your CC, your saves and the CC they use, your graphics settings, memory and start times.
perf.intro: Faster loading and less lag, with the same max graphics.
perf.gfx.text: Your graphics settings file decides how good the game looks and how much it lags.
perf.gfx.tuned_text: Everything still looks like your max graphics. Only the settings that caused lag were changed.
perf.gfx.lag_text: Your graphics file asks for more than the game can handle smoothly. One click fixes it and keeps max quality.
perf.gfx.stock_text: You're using the game's default graphics settings. There's nothing to fix.
perf.times.title: Start times
perf.times.text: The SpeedKit Monitor times every start, from pressing Play to the main menu.
perf.times.none: No start times yet. They appear here after you play through the Hub.
perf.chart: Start times, oldest on the left
perf.legend.fast: Faster starts (Quick Start, one save or Studio mode)
perf.lag.title: Find what makes your game lag
perf.lag.text: The SpeedKit Monitor has a built-in lag meter that shows which mods slow your game down.
perf.lag.s1: Load your game and go to a lot
perf.lag.s1_text: Play as usual, somewhere the game feels slow.
perf.lag.s2_text: The cheat console opens at the top of the screen.
perf.lag.s3_text: Then keep playing normally for one minute.
perf.lag.s4_text: A message in the game names the 5 mods that slow it down the most. A full report is saved to your Reports folder.
perf.lag.longer: For a longer test, type speedkit.lag 120 to measure for 2 minutes.
perf.lag.missing: The lag meter isn't in your game yet. It's added the next time you press Play.

care.patch.title: After a game update
care.patch.text: Game updates often break script mods until their creators release a fix. Script mods older than the latest game update are listed here.

care.patch.older.one: {n} script mod is older than the latest game update. Game updates often break script mods.
care.patch.older.other: {n} script mods are older than the latest game update. Game updates often break script mods.

care.patch.all_newer: All script mods are newer than the latest game update.
care.patch.note: An older file doesn't prove a mod is broken, and a newer file doesn't prove it's fixed. Setting a mod aside deletes nothing. The game stops loading it until you put it back or undo the change.

care.patch.show_older.one: Show the {n} script mod older than the last update
care.patch.show_older.other: Show the {n} script mods older than the last update

care.patch.aside_error: set aside {ago} because of an error
care.patch.newer_copy: a newer copy is in your Mods folder now
care.errors.title: Which mod caused this error?
care.errors.text: The game writes an error report when something goes wrong. Where possible, each error is matched to the mod behind it.
care.errors.order: Newest first. Repeated errors are shown once, with a count.
care.errors.empty: Error reports written by the game appear here.
care.error.ui: An error in the game's menus. Mods that change the menus can cause these.
care.error.game: The cause may be the game itself, or a mod that changes the game's files.
care.error.mentioned: the report mentions this mod, but it may not be the cause
care.load.title: How long the game takes to load
care.load.text: Time from pressing Play to the main menu, plus loading the save. Measured by the SpeedKit Monitor, typical value per mode.
care.load.saved: {mode}: about {time} less per start than Full Start
care.load.none: No start times recorded yet. The SpeedKit Monitor times every game start made through the Hub.
care.load.try_quick: Start once with Quick Start to compare.
care.load.try_full: Start once with Full Start to compare.
care.load.not_quicker: So far Quick Start hasn't been faster on this PC.
care.load.few: Based on only a few starts so far. The figures get more reliable with more starts.
care.backup.before_aside: Made on patch day, before mods were set aside
care.backup.none: No backups yet. A backup copies your saves and never changes them.
care.backup.title: Save backups
care.backup.text: Copies of every save, stored outside the game's folders. The newest {n} backups are kept, and one is made automatically before patch-day changes. Your saves are never changed.
care.aside.text: The game stops loading them until you put them back. Your saves are backed up first.

care.aside.extra.one: {n} file that belongs to them goes too.
care.aside.extra.other: {n} files that belong to them go too.

care.aside.undo: Nothing is deleted. You can put each mod back once it's updated, or undo the change on the Tools page.
care.aside_one.title: Set {name} aside?
care.aside_one.text: The game stops loading this mod until you put it back. Nothing is deleted.
care.aside_one.what: If the errors stop, this mod was the cause. Check for an update from its creator. You can put it back on this page or undo the change.
care.restore.title: Restore these saves?
care.restore.text: Your saves go back to how they were on {date}. Your current saves are backed up first.
care.restore.what: Saves created after this backup aren't changed. "Undo last change" on the Tools page brings back your current saves.
care.patch.aside_fix: set aside {ago} until it gets a Sims 4 Studio fix
bf.title: CC that may need a Sims 4 Studio fix
bf.text: Some game updates change how the game reads CC, and Sims 4 Studio's batch fixes update the files. This check reads your CC, lists the files that match a known problem and names the fix to run. Your CC files are never changed here.
bf.note: "May need" means a file matches a problem a batch fix is known for. It doesn't prove the item looks wrong in your game. Setting a file aside deletes nothing. You can put it back under "After a game update" or undo the change.

bf.line.one: {n} CC file may need a Sims 4 Studio fix ({fixes}).
bf.line.other: {n} CC files may need a Sims 4 Studio fix ({fixes}).

bf.step2: Open Sims 4 Studio (a recent version) and choose {path}.
bf.step3: Pick your Mods folder when asked. Sims 4 Studio keeps a copy of each file it changes.
bf.step4: Come back here and press Check again.

bf.parked_note.one: {n} of these files is parked by Quick Start or one-save mode. Switch to Full Start first so every file is in the Mods folder when the fix runs.
bf.parked_note.other: {n} of these files are parked by Quick Start or one-save mode. Switch to Full Start first so every file is in the Mods folder when the fix runs.

bf.open_title: Show this file in its folder

bf.aside.text.one: The game stops loading it until you put it back.
bf.aside.text.other: The game stops loading them until you put them back.

bf.aside.what: Nothing is deleted. Sims 4 Studio skips files that are set aside when it runs the fix on your Mods folder, so put them back first. You can undo this on the Tools page.
